_note: Verifiers are the checks the gates run (CANON.md ruling 16 as amended by ruling 17 of 2026-09-08: Claude writes them). Because the same party writes the tool and its check, each entry states the independent method or data the check rests on; a check that reuses the tool's own code is a stub with extra steps. The gate runner derives each status from the file on disk: missing (no file), stub (empty or carrying the '# STUB' marker), present; a present verifier is run as a gate step for its exit code.

verifiers.name: atlas_probe_check
verifiers.author: Codex
verifiers.checks: Legacy global elevation lookup, cell registration, source coverage, source hashes, invalid input refusal and deterministic output; a deliberately altered elevation report must fail in a separate verifier process.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: Enumerates geographic cell intervals and decodes signed values by byte arithmetic, against an asymmetric synthetic fixture and optionally the existing bake; the tool uses direct coordinate indexing and struct. Reference is WG.0a's cell-area law. Imports no probe code; validates the adapter, not geographic source accuracy.

verifiers.name: decode_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: One Terrarium tile decodes to metres that match a known pixel (elevation_m = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768).
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: the published Terrarium encoding applied by hand to a cached tile's pixels, and a pixel over open sea that must decode to about zero; never imports Tools/data/terrarium.py

verifiers.name: region_stats
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The baked heights raster's min, max and sea fraction are plausible; refuses zero rows. With --world, the world's heights layer gives the sea a floor between the datum and 30 m down that deepens with distance from the shore.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: reading the raw .r32 with numpy from the sidecar's stated shape alone, plausibility bounds for this coast taken from published relief rather than from the bake's own sidecar statistics, and for the world's sea floor its own Euclidean distance to the nearest land cell at sampled sea cells against the stated one-in-twenty rule

verifiers.name: summit_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Bherwerre Trig Point (170 m, a kilometre east of the box) reads as a summit in the surround and as the hill's flank in the region raster; the region's high ground is that hill and nowhere else; the east-west and north-south mirror images find only low ground; Jervis Bay and the ocean off Cave Beach are water; the ground north of a point behind Bherwerre Beach is land.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: coordinates and heights from Wikidata Q15107571, peakbagger.com, Parks Australia (booderee.gov.au) and beachesontheair.com, cited in the file, converted to raster cells by the frame rule the sidecar states rather than by the engine's code

verifiers.name: solar_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Sunrise, sunset, declination and the sun's place at the wake hour on day 237 at Bherwerre match an independent solar algorithm.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: the NOAA solar-position equations on the real date (Julian century, apparent ecliptic longitude, obliquity) against the engine's Spencer-series declination; the engine's line is read as text from the almanac tool, the engine is never imported

verifiers.name: station_table
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Parses hand-downloaded BoM CSVs for stations 068034 and 068072 into the calibration table.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: the Bureau's own CSVs, downloaded by the owner by hand because the Bureau blocks scripts (DEBTS.md); the table is checked against the station page by eye

verifiers.name: corpus_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Independently re-derives the corpus verdict from the raw result files and their mtimes, so the runner cannot grade itself.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: reading only the raw per-scenario result files and their modification times, never the runner's summary

verifiers.name: join_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Recomputes N1-N4, or one of them with --only, from the contracted run logs independently of the runner's own summary; since M1.5d N2's named segments are the bank, the shore, the cliff's top edge, the shore platform and the wade, and a walk that never reached one fails; since M1.7a N4's count row compares the entities each client holds inside its own and the other player's interest radius, second by second of the server's clock.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: recomputing every criterion from run.jsonl records alone, with the thresholds restated from CANON ruling 11 rather than imported from the harness

verifiers.name: drainage_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The engine's catchment layer agrees with an independent D8 at the two largest creeks and at the water gathered into Lake Windermere and Lake McKenzie, within 10 %.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: its own priority-flood fill (heapq), steepest-descent routing and height-ordered accumulation in numpy over the raw bake raster, seeded from the sea and the world's lake cells; never imports the engine or Tools/data; the lake points are Wikidata's (Q21908519, Q23759865)

verifiers.name: census_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The world's water and topology layers put Lake Windermere, Lake McKenzie, Blacks Waterhole and Ryans Swamp where the published sources do at the published sizes, the bay salt, Cave Beach a beach with dune behind it, the south-east shore hard, and say how far the chosen wake lies from Cave Beach.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: numpy over the layers' raw files with the frame rule the sidecars state; areas from Wikipedia (Jervis Bay Territory), positions and McKenzie's elevation from Wikidata, Cave Beach from Destination NSW (visitnsw.com), Steamers Head from Wikidata, the bay point from beachesontheair.com; the bake's outlines are OpenStreetMap's and only Blacks Waterhole's position falls back to them, which the row says

verifiers.name: species_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The world grows its plants where people have found them: for every plant with five or more usable Atlas of Living Australia records in the box, its share of the ground within 100 m of its records against its share of all the land, and the median distance from the sea of the world's plant against its records'; rows the world still fails are owed by name in DEBTS.md and fail the check the day they pass.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: occurrence records made by people in the field (the Atlas of Living Australia, fetched and cached by Tools/data/fetch_ala.py), laid on the world's layers in numpy by the frame rule the sidecar states, with planted specimens and records not placed to within 100 m dropped; never imports the engine, and matches the plants by the names the layers' own legends print

verifiers.name: save_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: A world folder holds what the server says: every region file's CRC and cell (versions 1 and 2), every player file's CRC (versions 2 and 3), what is carried out of the world (no carried id lying in a region file, beyond next_entity_id, or carried twice), every taking from the loose layer naming only things its cell held and kept in its own cell's file, and the world digest rebuilt by hand from the files, the hands' and the takings' lines among them, equals digest.txt.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: reading world.json, players/*.egp, regions/*.egr and digest.txt with Python alone by the layouts ARCHITECTURE section 10 states, rebuilding the digest's lines and FNV-1a 64 from them; never imports the engine or the server, so a writer that drifts from its stated format is caught by a reader that did not

verifiers.name: loading_check
verifiers.author: Codex
verifiers.checks: The built player keeps advancing during preparation, reaches play on new/continue, and reports missing data with a working return to menu.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: Python and Pillow read raw eg2.loading observations, existing run.jsonl, child exit codes and PNG pixel arrays; thresholds come from the written loading contract and ARCHITECTURE section 10, never from the launcher or recorder implementation. Visual layout is also inspected directly.

verifiers.name: tile_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: Every tile in a client's disk cache agrees with the world folder's own layer: the ground to half a centimetre, the surface put back from ground plus depth to two, the water's class, the ground's cover, what stands and what lies loose post for post; the far stand and the far count post for post against the stand's own squares, and the far layers holding the whole region with their counts adding up to the stand's trees; and the other layers inside the residency bound.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: inflating the cached bytes with zlib and reading them by the layouts ARCHITECTURE sections 7 and 10 state, including the tile grid's geometry and the cell a post sits on, restated in Python; never imports TileCodec, TileGrid or any game code, so a writer that drifts from its stated format is caught by a reader that did not; the far squares are counted over the whole raster at once in numpy, every cell into the one square it falls in, where the game works out each post's square on its own

verifiers.name: fauna_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The animals the server stood up round the founders, as its host logged them every ten seconds, against the world folder's own layers: none on open water or under the water's surface, every oystercatcher on the shore strip, every kangaroo within reach of fresh water, and for each kind the groups that stood in the squares wholly within reach against what the capacity layers put there, within three standard deviations and one group.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: reading the host's fauna records and the layers with Python and numpy by the layouts ARCHITECTURE section 10 states; the squares' mean capacities summed over the whole raster at once with bincount where the game adds a layer cell by cell, the dry share of each square counted from the water and surface layers, which the game never counts, and the expectation formed as a Bernoulli sum the game never forms; never imports presence, the stand-up or any game code

verifiers.name: cover_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The world's ground cover follows from the world's other layers: every post's cover by the cascade, every post's wetness quarter by the wetness layer, the posts no stored value can decide against what the storage steps predict, and the region's shares by cover with a floor under how varied the country must be.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: recomputing the cover in numpy from the water, topology, plant, soil and wetness layers by the cascade restated from the M1.4d contract as the M1.2b contract reorders it, with the plants' forms and the one pioneer held in the check from ECOSYSTEM.md and a species it does not know refused rather than guessed; never imports GroundCovers or any game code

verifiers.name: build_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: The client starts no streaming work in a frame whose 1.5 ms allowance is already spent; the preparation of a tile really runs off the main thread and the named Unity steps account for what the main thread spends; what is left is TerrainData.SetHeights and not something new growing beside it; every tile held was built. It prints the worst frame of streaming work beside the design frame and the named-defect line.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: reading run.jsonl alone -- the client's per-tile build records, not its own summary of itself -- and restating ARCHITECTURE section 8's budget, design frame and named-defect line as its own constants; it imports no game code and computes its own totals and shares

verifiers.name: stand_check
verifiers.author: Claude
verifiers.checks: What stands and lies on the ground follows the M1.6a rules: every trunk under its own canopy, no two nearer than their crowns allow, the crowns covering about what the canopy covers, heights inside each plant's range and the sand forest inside BioNet's 5-20 m, stems a hectare of each plant's canopy inside the design's band, sticks only under crowns, cobbles only where stone lies loose.
verifiers.independent_of_the_tool_by: numpy over the world's own layers by the codes their sidecars' legends state; the crown shares and height ranges restated from ECOSYSTEM.md's table and the sand forest's height from NSW BioNet's profile of Bangalay Sand Forest; never imports the engine, so a placement that drifts from the contract's rules is caught by a reader that did not drift with it
